Issued at 233 AM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

Today-Tonight...Stratiform showers continue to traverse the area
prior to sunrise, maintaining soggy conditions overnight. A quick
break looks possible towards sunrise. However, expect another day
of high coverage of showers with scattered embedded storms, with 
a stationary boundary draped across the county warning area.

Rinse and repeat today, as deep moisture remains present over the
Florida peninsula. Near record PWATs approaching 2.5" will
continue to support PoPs near 90% across the entire area. Multiple
rounds of showers and storms are once again expected, with the
front stalled near the Treasure Coast. Widespread, quick rainfall
totals of 2-4" are forecast, especially in deeper convection. 
CAMs suggest the greatest chance for a few storms (and likely the
highest totals) will be across southern portions of the area this
afternoon and into this evening. This will, of course, exacerbate
any ongoing flooding concerns from the recent rains. All of east 
central Florida is once again in a Marginal Risk (1/4) for 
excessive rainfall. Showers and storms look to move offshore in
the evening hours, though scattered showers will remain possible
north of I-4 overnight.

Northeasterly winds are forecast today north of the stalled front.
Winds generally remain under 10 mph or less through tonight,
though will need to monitor for an increase in winds along the
Volusia County coast later this afternoon and into tonight, as the
front begins to lift northward. Onshore flow along the Volusia
Coast is expected to produce a High Risk of rip currents and rough
surf at those beaches today. Entering the water in this area is
strongly discouraged. Dense cloud cover and high precipitation
coverage once again keeps highs in the lower 80s north of
Melbourne today. However, breaks in the clouds should allow for
areas to the south to reach the mid to upper 80s. Muggy conditions
will produce peak heat indices in the upper 90s to lower 100s
along the Treasure Coast.

Friday-Sunday...Ridging over the western Atlantic prevents Hurricane 
Isaias from reaching the Florida peninsula, while an upper level 
trough lifts the storm into the northern Gulf Coast late Friday into 
early Saturday. As the hurricane lifts northward, it finally
nudges our stationary front northward, though it remains over the
Southeast US through the weekend. Locally, onshore flow on Friday
veers southerly for the weekend and becomes breezy as the 
pressure gradient tightens. The breeziest conditions are forecast 
Saturday, with gusts 20-25 mph. PWATs diminish slightly (nearer to
2") on Friday as the front lifts northward, but increasingly 
southerly flow will once again advect deep tropical moisture into 
the area for the weekend. Thus, little change to the overall 
message of the forecast, with high PoPs 60-80% continuing late 
week and through Sunday. However, will see increasing breaks in 
between showers and storms Friday, but especially on Sunday, as 
drier air begins to move into the area from the south later in the
day. Rainfall totals Friday and Sunday are expected to be closer 
to 1-1.5" or less, though deeper convection Saturday once again 
leads to the possibility of widespread totals 1-3". Therefore, 
could see minor flooding concerns persist in areas that have 
received heavy rainfall over the last several days. The highest 
totals on Friday will likely be north of I-4, closer to the front 
as it lifts northward. That area remains in a Marginal Risk for 
excessive rainfall to end the week.

Increasing southerly flow advects warmer air into the forecast area, 
with high temperatures reaching the upper 80s to lower 90s by the 
weekend. More efficient daytime heating and additional breaks in 
the cloud cover will increase the chance for afternoon 
thunderstorms compared to the last several days. A few storms 
could be strong, producing wind gusts near 45 mph. Overnight lows 
look to remain in the mid to upper 70s. 

Monday-Thursday...The trough containing the remnants of Isaias moves 
off of the Northeast US coast early next week. Meanwhile, high 
pressure strengthens and stacks vertically over the northern Gulf 
Coast, moving eastward through the period. Locally, the weak front 
associated with the trough will drag southward through the peninsula 
on Monday. PWATs near 2" will continue to support scattered showers 
and storms (PoPs 20-30%) along the boundary. However, northerly 
winds behind the front will advect much drier air into the local 
area. PWATs fall below 1.5" (below 1" Tuesday), reducing PoPs to 20% 
or less Tuesday and Wednesday. Northerly flow prevails through mid-
week, as the ridge moves eastward, veering onshore late in the 
period. High temperatures overall remain in the upper 80s to near 
90. However, much less humid conditions Tuesday and Wednesday will 
limit heat indices to the lower to mid-90s. Overnight lows also dip 
into the 60s.
